analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the one who appears, and אֶל אַבְרָם identifies Abram as the one to whom he appears. The verse recalls the event in הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו, “who appeared to him.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a third-person masculine singular Niphal wayyiqtol. Its subject is יַהְוֶה.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרָא יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, Abram is the person to whom Yahweh appeared. The verse repeats this relation in הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו, “who appeared to him.”
analysis.morphology: Simple Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Marks the person to whom someone appears.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרָא יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, Abram is the person to whom Yahweh appears. Yahweh then addresses him directly in לְזַרְעֲךָ, “to your offspring.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding preposition אֶל is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: Yahweh promises Abram, “To your offspring I will give this land.” לְזַרְעֲךָ identifies the recipient, and אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת marks “this land” as the direct object of אֶתֵּן.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular. The initial אֶ־ marks the first person, and the dagesh in תּ reflects assimilation of the first root consonant נ.
analysis.sense: give land to someone as a possession

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.
